evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Never asked. Rep moved directly into logistics probing without asking about concerns like reliability or damage.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised by customer at step 2.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep did not address value days, cheaper day options, or date flexibility. Only asked 'You looking to move on a weekday, a weekend?' without follow-through on pricing differences.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep said 'I'll send everything over an email' and 'If you can give us a call of course or you can also reply to the email' but never explicitly asked for the business. No rate lock or no-deposit language. Rep treated this as a quote-send call rather than a close attempt.

top_strength: Jules gathered comprehensive logistics details efficiently — square footage, layout, bedroom count, item inventory (bed types, appliances, dressers, couch), box count, destination addresses and unit sizes — establishing a clear picture for accurate pricing.
coaching_note: This call skipped the two critical steps that close sales: never asked about customer concerns (step 2) or delivered the On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage promises (step 3), and abandoned the ask entirely — you handled this as a quote-send call, not a sales call. Restart with the two-concerns question right after the quid pro quo, deliver both promises before probing, and end with an explicit ask for the business rather than defaulting to email.
